lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Who Was Pablo Picasso?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about Picasso's life from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about Picasso.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a Picasso painting and discuss initial reactions.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about Picasso's life and style.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Look up a Picasso painting together.

lessons.title: Shapes in Picasso's Cubist Style
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify 2D shapes within a cubist artwork.
success_criteria: I can name shapes in the artwork.
I can describe their properties.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a cubist Picasso painting.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model identifying 2D shapes (triangles, rectangles, circles) used in cubist style artwork.
lessons.independent_task: Children identify and record shapes in a Picasso artwork, describing properties.
key_questions: How many sides does this shape have?

differentiation.greater_depth: Identify multiple shapes and compare properties

lessons.assessment_notes: Note shape recognition applied to an art analysis context — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.plenary: Recap shapes identified in the artwork.
lessons.home_link: Look for shapes in a picture or painting at home.

lessons.title: Studying Picasso's Cubist Style
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of Picasso's cubist style.
success_criteria: I can describe what I notice in a Picasso painting.
I can name a feature of cubism.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a cubist Picasso portrait.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss features of cubism — fragmented shapes, multiple viewpoints shown at once, angular forms.
lessons.independent_task: Children describe what they notice in a Picasso painting, recording their observations.
key_questions: What do you notice about the face in this painting?

differentiation.support: Point to and describe one feature
differentiation.greater_depth: Describe multiple features and give an opinion

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational and descriptive skill studying an artist — evidence for ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Look at more Picasso paintings together if possible.

lessons.title: Writing About a Picasso Painting
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write sentences describing what they see in a Picasso painting.
success_criteria: I can write what I see.
I can use a describing word.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing descriptive sentences about a Picasso painting.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences describing a Picasso artwork.
key_questions: What can you see in the painting?
What shapes and colours are used?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive writing about visual art — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share painting descriptions with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Describe a picture or painting at home.

lessons.title: Position and Direction: Cubist Faces
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use positional language to describe features in a cubist-style face.
success_criteria: I can describe where a feature is.
I can use positional words.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap positional language from earlier terms.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using positional language to describe features in a cubist-style face (e.g. 'the eye is above the nose').
lessons.independent_task: Children describe features in a cubist artwork using positional language.
key_questions: Can you use a positional word?

differentiation.support: Use simple positional words with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note cross-curricular application of positional language to art — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Describe positions of things in a room at home.

lessons.title: Creating a Cubist-Style Self-Portrait
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a self-portrait in a simplified cubist style.
success_criteria: I can rearrange facial features in a cubist way.
I can use bold shapes.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap cubism features discussed on Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a simplified cubist-style self-portrait, rearranging features using bold shapes.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own cubist-style self-portrait.
key_questions: How will you rearrange your features?
What bold shapes will you use?

differentiation.greater_depth: Create an original composition with multiple viewpoints

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe application of a specific artist's technique — evidence for ART.1/ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Look at how faces are drawn in different styles together.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Art Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read art-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read art words.
I can read a sentence about art.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to art-themed words (e.g. 'shape', 'colour', 'paint').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading art words over the week.

lessons.title: Art-Themed Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using an art context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using an art context (e.g. paintbrushes/colours used).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve art-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up an art-themed word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Picasso-Inspired Animal Collage
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create an animal collage inspired by Picasso's simplified line drawings.
success_criteria: I can create a simplified animal shape.
I can use bold lines.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at Picasso's simple line drawings of animals (e.g. his dove or owl sketches).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a simplified animal collage using bold shapes and lines, inspired by Picasso's economical drawing style.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own simplified animal collage.
key_questions: How can you simplify this animal's shape?
What bold lines will you use?

differentiation.greater_depth: Create a detailed composition with multiple simplified elements

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe application of a simplification technique inspired by an artist — evidence for ART.1/ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Try drawing a simplified animal shape at home.

lessons.title: Presenting Our Picasso-Inspired Art
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present their Picasso-inspired artwork and explain their inspiration.
success_criteria: I can describe my artwork.
I can say what inspired me.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Picasso's style studied this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation about artwork.
lessons.independent_task: Children present their cubist self-portrait or animal collage to a small group.

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and art reflection progress — evidence for ENG.SL1/ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Present your artwork to your family.

lessons.title: Fractions in Picasso's Compositions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply fraction knowledge to describe proportions in an artwork.
success_criteria: I can say a fraction relates to part of an artwork.
I can use fraction language.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using fraction language to describe proportions within a Picasso composition (e.g. 'about half the painting is blue').
lessons.independent_task: Children use fraction language to describe proportions in their own or Picasso's artwork.
key_questions: What fraction of the painting is this colour?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of fractions to a creative/visual context — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Estimate a fraction of colour in a picture at home.

lessons.title: Comparing Picasso to Artists Studied Before
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare Picasso's style to another artist studied previously.
success_criteria: I can name a similarity.
I can name a difference.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap other artists studied (Rousseau, Warhol from Year 1).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing Picasso's cubist style to a previously studied artist's style.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare Picasso to another artist, recording similarities and differences.
key_questions: What is similar about these styles?

differentiation.support: Compare with adult support, one similarity/difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative art analysis skill, building across years — evidence for ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Look at two different artists' work together if possible.

lessons.title: Pablo Picasso Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about Pablo Picasso.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about Picasso.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about Picasso, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why might he have painted faces in unusual ways?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on Picasso facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Shape, Position, Fractions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply shape, position and fraction skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name shapes.
I can use positional language.
I can estimate fractions.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of shape, position, and fractions.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 29 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.GEO/N4.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising shape properties over the weekend.

lessons.title: Pablo Picasso Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about Pablo Picasso and cubism.
success_criteria: I can describe cubism.
I can name a technique I tried.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about Picasso.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review and contribute to a class 'Pablo Picasso' display featuring their cubist-inspired art.
key_questions: What have we learned about Picasso?
What was your favourite technique to try?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note artist study progress, an ongoing Year 2 objective — evidence for ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about Picasso with your family.
